en.title: Find a Matrix Element That Is the Maximum of Its Row and the Minimum of Its Column
en.description:
The matrix elements are non-negative. Find an element that equals both the maximum of its row and the minimum of its column, and output its value; if none exists, output −1. Multiple equal maximum or minimum positions are all valid; it does not need to be strictly greater or smaller.

See the input protocol for this site's supplements to missing ranges and its recovery of typos in the source.
en.input: The first line contains N M, followed by N lines of M integers each. Original bounds: 1≤N,M≤1000; the elements are non-negative but have no upper bound, so this site adds ≤10^9. The next sentence of the original input swapped the dimensions as M rows and N columns; this site restores N rows and M columns based on the explicit dimension definition.
en.output: Output a single integer, the answer.
en.explanation: The outputs of the three public examples are, in order: 2; 1; -1. Verified by independent enumeration or direct simulation.
hints: Process the matrix row by row, recording the minimum of each column and the minimum R over all row maxima. Let C be the maximum of the column minima; if R=C, output that value, otherwise output −1. Keep only M column values, and do not build a copy of a million-integer matrix.
